leaderboard.style: wordless image meme, no caption; hit the Elon GPU-hire thread (35 likes) and the r/OpenSource ban thread (195 likes) inside one 05:14-05:18 UTC burst, and the same burst also topped the smaller a16z GPU-chart thread

patterns: One-liners win Elon threads and land in the first 1-7 minutes: emoji, slogan, or a three-word jab. The highest single reply in the set is still a one-liner, Tim Sweeney’s “Redditors.” at 1015 likes.
Joke-reuse of the parent’s noun beats fresh argument. “Stranded Compute” as a punk-band name (387) and “forgot to include make no mistakes” (1090) both peaked near +56m.

Genuine expertise is rare and later. The only operational question in an Elon top-reply slot is Mike Alfred’s 200k-GPUs-a-month ask at +1h4m (121). Design critique on the landing-page post arrived at +2h to +7h and stayed under 30 likes.
Contrarian one-liners sit in the +20m to +2h band: the $40B borrow jab, the “AI over-designed homepages” slam, Emad’s “few quarters too early.”
Verbatim quote of the parent is almost absent. The near case is “Sarah Friar said this verbatim,” a citation flex, not a paste of the post.
Length: every reply above 100 likes is under roughly 120 characters, except the GPU-capacity question. Long replies did not crack a top-five.
Timing splits by post type. Promo and quote-tweets crown inside 15 minutes. Controversy (open-source ban, neolab GPU resale) crowns at 5-8 hours. Elon’s own reply outliked Yuchen’s parent by +8h17m.

sama, karpathy, simonw, OpenAI, and Anthropic had no post in this window that cleared the cut. swyx’s only post was a hiring note at 198 likes. The visible AI conversation was Grok, GPU scarcity, and one anti-AI moderation fight.
No text reply-guy repeated across these eight threads. The only multi-thread top replier is an image account posting silent memes in a four-minute burst.
